summary: Iter 17 — Definitive image-health + scroll-to-hash + admin iframe testing at 1440x900. FINDINGS: (1) IMAGES on 7/8 routes are FULLY working (landing 17 imgs 0 broken; barsaat 1/1; naani-ghar 5/5; about-the-chef 3/3; menus 2/2; menus/naani-ghar 0 imgs; menus/barsaat 0 imgs; suppers 2/2). Zero 4xx to /artifacts/ URLs across all routes. User's claim 'none of the images are visible' is FALSE for all standard site content EXCEPT the Gallery section (see #2). (2) ❌ GALLERY on / is BROKEN — 13 total items: 5 images + 8 videos. Of the 5 images, 1 is BROKEN because the src is a local Windows file path 'file:///C:/Users/shahv/Downloads/drive-download-20260701T140349Z-3-001/DSC01724.jpg' — this URL will never load in any browser (bug in seeded gallery data). Of the 8 videos, ALL 8 show readyState=0 and after forced .load() give MediaError code 4 (SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED); visually the gallery grid shows 8 black/empty cells with only a small '▷ VIDEO' label. HEAD requests to the same MP4 URLs return HTTP 200 + content-type video/mp4, so URLs are correct — the failure is inside the browser (likely CORS on Range requests, missing poster attribute, or preload='none' + no click-to-play). This is almost certainly what the user means by 'no images visible' — 9 of 13 gallery cells (~70%) are visually blank. Also, gallery has 13 items in DOM, not 12 as stated in review request. (3) ❌ SCROLL-TO-HASH FIX NOT APPLIED — Main agent claimed to switch to behavior:auto + 800ms settling re-scroll, but /app/frontend/src/App.js line 33 STILL reads `el.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' });` with NO follow-up re-scroll. Test results identical to iter 16: from /supper-club/barsaat click nav-gallery → after 4s #gallery.top=2344 (spec requires -50..400) ❌; nav-contact → #contact.top=4107 ❌. (4) /admin/edit iframe (loads /?preview=draft): 18 imgs, 6 flagged as nw=0 at check time — 1 real (the same file:/// path from bug #2), 5 are transient (duplicates of already-working artifact URLs, i.e. nw=0 because they're still lazy-loading below the fold at check time — HEAD returns 200 OK).

ui_bugs.issue: One gallery image has a local Windows file path as src ('file:///C:/Users/shahv/Downloads/drive-download-20260701T140349Z-3-001/DSC01724.jpg') — will never load in browser, results in permanent blank cell. Fix by re-uploading DSC01724.jpg to /artifacts/ and updating the MongoDB gallery record.

All 8 gallery videos render as black/empty cells labeled '▷ VIDEO' — readyState stays at 0 and manual .load() triggers MediaError code 4 (SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED). But direct HEAD to same URLs returns HTTP 200 with content-type video/mp4. Root cause is likely (a) missing poster attribute so nothing is shown until user clicks, and/or (b) preload='metadata' with a CORS/Range issue on customer-assets CDN preventing metadata fetch. Combined with #gallery-image bug above, this makes 9/13 gallery cells (~70%) visually blank — exactly matching user's 'no images visible' complaint.

integration_issues.issue: Main agent's claimed fix was NOT applied. /app/frontend/src/App.js line 33 still uses behavior:'smooth' with no settling re-scroll. From /supper-club/barsaat clicking [data-testid=nav-gallery] lands #gallery.top=2344 (spec requires -50..400). Same failure for nav-contact → #contact.top=4107. Fix required: change 'smooth' to 'auto' AND/OR add setTimeout(()=>el.scrollIntoView({behavior:'auto',block:'start'}), 800) after the first call, exactly as recommended in iter-16 report.

action_items: FIX GALLERY IMAGE with file:// URL — DSC01724.jpg has src='file:///C:/Users/shahv/Downloads/...'. Re-upload the file to customer-assets and update MongoDB gallery collection.

FIX GALLERY VIDEOS not rendering — add poster attribute (thumbnail) to each <video>, set preload='metadata' minimum, and verify CORS. Direct URLs work (HTTP 200). Investigate why browser gives MediaError.code=4 despite valid MP4 headers. Consider serving a JPEG poster from same CDN.

APPLY THE SCROLL-TO-HASH FIX that was CLAIMED but not made — in /app/frontend/src/App.js line 33 change `{ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' }` to `{ behavior: 'auto', block: 'start' }` AND add a follow-up `setTimeout(()=>{const e2=document.querySelector(hash); if(e2)e2.scrollIntoView({behavior:'auto',block:'start'});}, 800);` right after the successful scroll call.
